entry.title: Combined summary - Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary: Over the past two years, the Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) repository has experienced a notable resurgence in activity and process refinement. A team of six BIP Editors undertook a comprehensive effort to manage and develop the repository, leaving thousands of comments, processing hundreds of pull requests, and facilitating the publication of dozens of new BIPs. These initiatives led to a more active submission environment and fostered dynamic discussions among Bitcoin developers. Key advancements included the creation of a new BIP Process, important updates to existing documentation, systematic resolution of abandoned proposals, and improvements in continuous integration workflows. While these accomplishments have positively shaped the repository’s direction, the operational workload often became concentrated on a single individual, highlighting the demanding nature of editorial responsibilities and leading to a reevaluation of optimal team size. A smaller editorial group—ideally three engaged members—has been identified as a more effective structure for managing the BIPs repository. This approach encourages collaboration while ensuring accountability and streamlined decision-making. Recognition is extended to editors who have contributed both publicly and behind the scenes, notably Murch, whose dedication significantly improved the repository’s organization and efficiency. Active participation and thoughtful contributions from all team members have proven essential to sustaining the project’s momentum. Interest in joining the editorial team continues to grow, with individuals such as Jaroslav Dlouhy expressing a willingness to formalize their involvement. Jaroslav seeks clarification on the requirements needed to complete his authorization and demonstrates sustained commitment, having previously volunteered to support the initiative. His engagement exemplifies the proactive spirit valued within the community. The role of a BIP Editor requires deep technical knowledge of the Bitcoin protocol, experience with programming languages commonly used in the ecosystem like C++ or Python, and familiarity with collaborative open-source development practices. Essential skills include proficiency with version control systems such as Git and strong written communication abilities. Qualified candidates are typically expected to have prior involvement in Bitcoin projects or protocol design and must demonstrate meticulous attention to detail. The editorial position demands a weekly commitment of five to ten hours, focusing on tasks such as monitoring pull requests, prompting proposal owners for reviews, merging approved changes, and providing feedback on new BIPs. Most editorial functions, apart from labeling and merging pull requests, remain accessible to any interested community member, encouraging broad participation in reviewing and commenting on ongoing work. Aspiring contributors can explore open pull requests at [this link](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Apr+-label%3A%22Metadata+Update%22+-label%3ATypo-to-be-collected+-label%3ACI). Participation in BIP review is open to the wider community, with emphasis placed on providing constructive feedback and engaging in the iterative development process. Such involvement not only supports the quality of the repository but also helps identify future editorial candidates. The pace of review and discussion can be gradual, rewarding those who demonstrate consistent, valuable input over time. Despite these efforts, the editorial workload remains substantial. High-quality submissions often await review for prolonged periods, exacerbated when editors are unavailable due to personal commitments. To attract skilled volunteers, flexibility regarding term length is encouraged, with limited service durations of 12 to 24 months proposed as an alternative to indefinite commitments. This approach aims to reduce barriers for qualified candidates who may hesitate to assume long-term obligations. Upholding rigorous standards throughout the BIP process is recognized as essential for the progression of the Bitcoin protocol. Rather than compromising on review quality to address resource constraints, the editorial team seeks regular renewal through the inclusion of dedicated contributors. Increased support is being channeled towards the BIP process, with more structured allocation of working hours and a focus on peer review practices inspired by academic research. Recent collaborative priorities include output descriptors, Miniscript (explored in [Inside a Vinteum Deep Dive: The Standards Behind Bitcoin Wallets](https://www.vinteum.org/blog/inside-a-vinteum-deep-dive-the-standards-behind-bitcoin-wallets)), and Stratum V2 (detailed in [Inside a Vinteum Deep Dive: Bitcoin Mining from Protocol to Silicon](https://www.vinteum.org/blog/inside-a-vinteum-deep-dive-bitcoin-mining-from-protocol-to-silicon)). Contributors like Daniela Brozzoni have been acknowledged for their editorial diligence and steadfast commitment to maintaining clarity and precision in BIP specifications. Daniela Brozzoni stands out as a promising candidate for the role of BIP editor. As the author of BIP 394 and an active participant in the enhancement of BIP 360, she brings direct experience with the BIP process and its standards. While pursuing advanced academic studies focused on blockchain, Daniela commits significant time to reviewing Bitcoin Core contributions, as reflected in her [GitHub activity](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reviewed-by%3Ajeanpablojp).
